findings.title: Acquired support turns against its claimants
findings.claim: The beings taken as gods in 19:81 are meant to become strength for their takers; in 19:82 those same beings will repudiate the worship bond and become a contrary side against them, reversing the intended support relation.
findings.mechanism: The purpose clause لِيَكُونُوا لَهُمْ عِزًّا sets the intended outcome. The repeated becoming frame in يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدًّا turns that projected strengthening outward into opposition, while كَلَّا and the repudiation of worship mark the reversal.
findings.reader_payoff: The adjacent purpose and outcome clauses make the failed patronage legible as a reversal of direction: what was taken to strengthen the worshippers becomes adverse to them.
findings.containment: This reads the stated purpose beside the stated outcome; it does not make the intended gods literally enslaved, equally powerful, or the lexical meaning of either ك ف ر or ضِدًّا. Whether the verse asserts a causal consequence of the worship relation or corrects the expectation remains open.

epistemic.reason: The 19:81–82 purpose/outcome structure and trusted channel evidence are explicit, while the more precise reversal mechanism is also carried by a legacy_unbound HFT trace.

findings.mechanism: The supplied root trace places ك ف ر with the denier in 19:77, shifts it to the future plural worship recipients in 19:82 with worship as its governed object, and labels the pressured group كَافِرِينَ in 19:83. That recurrence and subject shift make the focus's disavowal resonate with the earlier denial.
findings.reader_payoff: The word for denial is heard as a returning action: the people who rejected signs face a repudiation of the worship relation they had constructed.
findings.containment: The root recurrence and subject shift are explicit in the supplied trace; a rhetorical rebound is an inference. The verses do not state that every use of ك ف ر is a deliberate reciprocal pun, and the focus's local denial reading remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace aligns with the supplied Arabic and focus return, but its reciprocal rhetorical force remains attributed under legacy_unbound provenance.

findings.containment: The packet does not state that 19:96 is a direct answer to 19:82 or that either outcome causes the other. The contrast remains contextual and does not decide who belongs to either group.

findings.title: A collective opposition faces solitary arrival
findings.claim: The plural subject of the focus becomes one contrary predicate, while the later accounting culminates in each person arriving alone. The passage can therefore be read as a collective adverse side set against individually accounted people.
findings.mechanism: Counting in 19:84, exhaustive enumeration in 19:94, and the singular arrival فَرْدًا in 19:95 provide the independent numerical and individualizing cues. They return through the focus's plural subject and singular ضِدًّا, making the opposition legible as one side facing persons who stand alone.
findings.reader_payoff: The singular predicate no longer reads only as a label for several separate enemies; against the later solitary arrival it can gather them into one adverse side.
findings.containment: This is a contextual geometry, not a claim that the opponent group is equal in status or that 19:95 addresses only worshippers. Counting may describe divine administration without specifying the geometry of opposition.

epistemic.reason: The HFT coordinates match counting, enumeration, solitude, and the focus; the collective-side inference remains attributed, and its equality branch was excluded.

branch_activations.activation: Total enumeration and singular arrival contact the focus's plural-to-singular relation.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The group is read inside an accounting sequence that culminates in individual arrival.
branch_activations.boundary: No independent gloss or facet is supplied for this branch in the packet.

findings.title: Opposition echoes a later cosmic rupture
findings.claim: The focus's incompatible opposition can be heard against the later image of the heavens nearly splitting, the earth splitting, and the mountains falling: the pericope lets a personal contrary relation echo as structural rupture.
findings.mechanism: The focus supplies the incompatible relation ضِدًّا, while 19:90 supplies successive images of fissuring, splitting, and collapse. Their contact moves the reader from an adverse relation between parties to an analogy of strain extending through the created order.
findings.reader_payoff: The later rupture gives the focus's opposition a scale beyond personal hostility, while remaining an image in the surrounding passage.
findings.containment: The later rupture is not claimed as a consequence caused by the worship in 19:82; it is retained only as a structural analogy within the pericope. The focus's ordinary adversarial reading remains available.

epistemic.reason: The surface coordinates and attributed HFT roles match, but extending the focus relation to cosmic rupture is explicitly exploratory.

findings.title: Opposition as filled relational space
findings.claim: The singular opposition predicate is available for a spatial probe: the focus's plural subjects become one contrary side, while crowding, gathering, and universal scope later in the passage make that side imaginable as filling the relational field.
findings.mechanism: The singular ضِدًّا after a plural subject supplies the focus carrier. The adjacent agitation image, the gathering toward the Merciful, and the later universal totality independently provide compression, concentration, and exhaustive-scope cues; together they make a space-filling analogy perceptible.
findings.reader_payoff: Opposition can be imagined as leaving no unoccupied pocket of patronage, rather than as several disconnected adversaries.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory spatial analogy, not the lexical meaning of ضِدًّا and not a literal container. The focus's ordinary adversarial reading remains intact; the contextual images may instead concern separate acts and groups.

epistemic.reason: The trace is coordinate-complete but its vessel-filling branch is explicitly branch-distant and the resulting spatial picture remains exploratory.

findings.title: Exclusive devotion redirects the help relation
findings.claim: With the added 1:5 overlay, the focus's worship language is read against worship and aid addressed to God alone: 19:81 says the taken gods were meant to be strength for their takers, while 1:5 gives worship and seeking help one exclusive addressee.
findings.mechanism: The focus's عِبَادَتِهِمْ supplies the carrier. The external ayah independently pairs fronted exclusive address with نَعْبُدُ and نَسْتَعِينُ; the native 19:81 purpose clause supplies the attempted strength relation. Their contact changes the comparison from patronage that fails into a question of where worship and aid are directed.
findings.reader_payoff: The contrast joins devotion and dependence: the beings taken to provide strength are set beside an explicit address to the one worshipped and asked for help.
findings.containment: This external ayah is an overlay that supplies a local contrast, not evidence that 19:82 quotes or directly depends on 1:5. It does not identify every focus subject or settle the meaning of opposition.

epistemic.reason: The word and relation contacts are explicit in the supplied Arabic, but the cross-ayah comparison is an editorial overlay rather than an explicit link.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The added 1:5 says worship and seeking aid are directed to You alone, while 19:81 states that the acquired gods were taken as strength.
branch_activations.activation: Exclusive worship and aid in the overlay meet the focus's worship bond and the native purpose clause, specifying the direction of dependence.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The attempted worship-and-strength relation is contrasted with direct worship and help-seeking addressed to God alone.
branch_activations.boundary: The overlay does not establish direct textual dependence or make the focus a quotation of 1:5.

branch_activations.activation: The focus's directed worship of acquired gods meets the overlay's exclusive address and aid relation, making the misdirection of patronage visible.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The same worship relation is set beside an explicit single addressee for worship and help.
branch_activations.boundary: The extension retains its core facet; this contrast does not determine every referent in the focus.

friction_notes: The focus word-alignment bridge resolves all 8 of 8 analysis entries; no focus carrier is lost to an unresolved join. HFT word/root roles remain attributed because their source trust is legacy_unbound.
The 19:83 pressure scene names Satans as its agents and does not establish that they are the same beings as the acquired gods in 19:81–82.
The 19:90 cosmic rupture is retained only as a structural analogy; no causal result of the focus's worship is claimed.
Among the added ayat 1:2–1:7, 1:5 alone supplies a focus-facing worship/aid contact that adds a local overlay; the other added ayat do not change a focus reading beyond the native pericope.
